title: Componentwise multiplication on ideal-power products
statement: For each m,k and homogeneous b of degree k, there exists a module-sheaf morphism G_m → G_(m+k) satisfying the displayed coefficient formula on every open and section.

proof.text: Set a equal to the degree-k coefficient of b. By mem_reesAlgebra_iff, a belongs to I^k. Use the existing Scheme.Modules.smulHom endomorphism, multiplying on each open by the restriction of the global section f-sharp(a).

The existing closed ideal_comap_appLE implementation, ideal_top_ofIdealTop and Ideal.map_map identify J(U) with the extension of I along the displayed coefficient map for every affine U. Ideal.map_pow therefore puts f-sharp(a) in J(U)^k.

Positive ideal powers are quasi-coherent and their affine inclusion ranges are J(U)^n by the ideal-times-quasi-coherent affine-section theorem. At n=0 the power inclusion is the identity of the structure sheaf, whose quasi-coherence is the existing isQuasicoherent_unit instance. Tensor-section bijectivity and the affine image-section formula show that each product inclusion has the additive subgroup generated by pure products as its affine range. Transfer the abelian-image formula to the chosen image using imageIsoImage.

Induct on the additive subgroup generated by pure products. Multiplication by f-sharp(a) preserves the target subgroup: on a pure product d times t, its new coefficient belongs to J(U)^k J(U)^m = J(U)^(m+k), hence lifts to a section of the target ideal power. Zero, addition and negation are preserved by scalar multiplication.

Compose the source inclusion followed by Scheme.Modules.smulHom with the target cokernel projection. The affine range inclusion makes this composite zero on every affine open; separatedness on the affine basis makes it zero globally. Apply kernel.lift, then the inverse of Abelian.factorThruImage for the monomorphic target inclusion. The kernel equation gives the factorization through the target inclusion, and evaluating this equation proves the coefficient formula on every open.

proof_origin.note: Existing Scheme.Modules.smulHom scalar morphism, affine range preservation, and abelian kernel factorization. Uses the closed affine extension implementation directly instead of modulePullbackIdealQuotient. No new statements or holes.

lean.statement:
theorem idealPowersReesMultiplication_component {A : Type v} [CommRing A]
    {X : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A))
    (I : Ideal A) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom)).comap f)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    let G := fun m ↦ Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι m).2 F
    let graded := reesGrading I
    ∀ (m k : ℕ) (b : graded k), ∃ mu : G m ⟶ G (m + k),
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : (G m).val.obj (op U)),
        ((Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι (m + k)).2 F).app
          U).hom ((mu.app U) s) =
        (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ U le_top).hom
          (b.val.val.coeff k)) •
        ((Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι m).2 F).app
          U).hom s
